name: Cryptic crossword No 26,474
preamble: Note added 21 January 2015: the clue for 8 across has been corrected since publication

clue.text: Leading expert got rogue virus, too

indicators.note: a rogue thing is out of control and behaves unpredictably, so the letters run wild into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A top specialist has caught a nasty computer or medical virus as well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rogue virus' reads as a phrase, but 'rogue' works on both 'virus' and 'too' together.
explanation.definitionFit: A virtuoso is a performer of outstanding skill, someone at the very top of a field.

clue.text: Slapper is a lap dancer, foremost

indicators.note: a dancer moves about, so these letters step into a different arrangement

blocks.note: the three letters rearranged
read as 'fore' plus 'most': the front letter of 'most'

explanation.surface: A cheeky picture of a lap dancer described in coarse slang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slapper' is British slang for a promiscuous woman, but here it is literally the thing that slaps. 'Foremost' splits into 'fore' plus 'most'.
explanation.definitionFit: The flat inner surface of the hand is what delivers a smack, so it is literally the part that does the slapping.

clue.text: Close dossier about an uprising

indicators.note: in a down entry, something rising reads from bottom to top, so the letters run backwards
to be about something is to surround it, so one piece wraps round the other

blocks.note: a dossier is a file of documents
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone shuts a dossier concerning a rebellion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close' looks like a verb meaning shut, but it is the noun: the close of a show. In a down clue an uprising reads bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: A finale is the closing part of a performance or piece of music, its ending.

clue.text: Bitter controversy on both sides at tax payable — albeit cut back

indicators.note: the two sides of a word are its edges, so only the outermost letters are kept
cutting back a word trims it from its tail end, leaving only its start

blocks.note: the first and last letters
NIC, National Insurance Contributions, is a UK payroll tax
a deletion: the word is cut back to its first two letters, dropping the last four

explanation.surface: A bitter row over tax owed, with some spending cuts thrown in.
explanation.walkthrough: NIC stands for National Insurance Contributions, a deduction from British wages; it is the least familiar chunk here.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone cynical is jaded and distrustful, and that sour outlook is close to being bitter.

clue.text: Accidentally refasten small opening

indicators.note: doing something by accident means getting it wrong, so the letters end up out of order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone clumsily does up a little gap again.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is anatomical Latin, from the word for window, so it may be unfamiliar; the letters of the second word give it exactly.
explanation.definitionFit: In anatomy and biology a fenestra is a small window-like aperture, such as the ones in the middle ear.

clue.text: Spokesperson for 12

definitions.note: refers to the answer at 12 across, TONGUE

blocks.note: first meaning: someone who speaks on behalf of another
second meaning: read literally, a piece of the mouth, which the answer at 12 across is

explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference points to TONGUE at 12 across: a tongue is literally a mouth piece, and it also speaks for its owner.
explanation.definitionFit: A mouthpiece is someone who voices another's views, and split in two it describes an organ inside the head.

clue.text: Knight's resting place is about all that remains

indicators.note: to turn about is to face the other way, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: a knight's title
somewhere to lie down

explanation.surface: A knight's tomb is the only thing left of him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resting place' suggests a grave, but it is simply a bed; the knight's bed, SIR BED, reads backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Debris is the scattered rubble and fragments left after destruction, the leftover remnants.

clue.text: Clinton, say, gets around it with glee

indicators.note: to get around something is to encircle it, so one piece goes outside the other

blocks.note: Hillary Clinton, with the first name trimmed to one L; 'say' flags an example
taken as written

explanation.surface: A politician merrily travels about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clinton' makes you think of Bill; the wordplay wants a first name spelt HILARY with one L, which is the usual spelling of the name even though Mrs Clinton uses two.
explanation.definitionFit: Hilarity is loud amusement and merriment, which is what glee means.

clue.text: Bring forth this woman before any other to get the go-ahead

indicators.note: getting something means receiving it and holding it within, so a piece is taken inside

blocks.note: in Genesis, Eve was the first woman
approval, permission

explanation.surface: A woman is first in line for permission to produce something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Before any other' sounds like a queue, but it means the first woman of all, from the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: To evoke something is to call it up or summon it, such as a memory or feeling.

clue.text: Couple with some intention to entertain marriage?

indicators.note: only some of each word is used, namely its opening letter

blocks.note: the initial letters of these four words

explanation.surface: A pair of lovers who are thinking about getting married.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer, an attempt at an &lit: a romantic pair who might be considering marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Two people publicly in a relationship are called an item in informal speech.

clue.text: A new mail entry cut important passage

indicators.note: making something new means remaking it, so these letters are rebuilt in a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
a canal is a cut, an artificial waterway dug through land

explanation.surface: An edited new postal item removed a key passage of text.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passage' suggests a piece of writing; it is a bodily tube. A cut is also a canal, as in the British waterways once called cuts.
explanation.definitionFit: The alimentary canal is the whole digestive tract from mouth to anus, a vital channel through the body.

clue.text: Spit on the 11 25

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for a thing found on the alimentary canal

blocks.note: first meaning: a narrow point of land running out into the sea
second meaning: an organ at the start of the digestive tract

explanation.walkthrough: 'Spit' tempts you towards saliva, which fits the mouth theme, but it is the geographical sense: a narrow strip of land jutting into water.
explanation.definitionFit: A tongue of land is a long projecting strip, and the muscular organ in the mouth sits at the entrance of the digestive tract.

clue.text: Earthquake could entail this regular payment

definitions.text: Earthquake could entail this regular payment

blocks.note: surface reading: a tremor causes some consequence
setter's reading: an earthquake tears the earth apart, and read that way the two words name a periodic charge

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer and read it literally: the earth is torn open in a quake. Ground rent is the regular fee a leaseholder pays the freeholder for the land, a British property arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Ground rent is a recurring sum paid by a leaseholder to the owner of the land beneath a building.

clue.text: This type of bet not as potent

indicators.note: saying the letters are not as they stand means they must be put in some other order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A kind of wager said to be weaker than another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not as potent' reads as a comparison, but 'not' is the only signal to rearrange, which is unusual. An ante-post bet is British racing jargon for a wager placed days before the race.
explanation.definitionFit: Ante-post describes a wager struck well in advance of the event, before the final runners are declared.

clue.text: Return of major river's agitated state just down from London Bridge

indicators.note: a return is a journey back, so the letters are read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: the Ob is a great Siberian river
a rough sea is an agitated one

explanation.surface: A big river runs back in turmoil below a famous London crossing.
explanation.walkthrough: The Borough is the district of Southwark at the south end of London Bridge, home of Borough Market; 'major river' is a hint at the Ob rather than the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: Borough is the name of the Southwark area immediately south of the bridge, with its market and tube station.

clue.text: Spout a lot of wind about railway getting green light

indicators.note: to be about something is to surround it, so the outer piece is wrapped round the rest
to get something is to take it in, so the inner piece is received inside

blocks.note: a strong wind
the standard abbreviation for railway
permission to proceed

explanation.surface: Someone talks endless hot air about a railway line being approved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spout a lot of wind' reads as talk nonsense, but 'Spout' is the noun definition. The railway takes in the go-ahead, and the wind goes round both.
explanation.definitionFit: A gargoyle is a carved grotesque on a building that channels rainwater from the roof out through its mouth.

clue.text: Dog's home opening now jeopardised by current reduction

indicators.note: an opening is where something begins, so each word gives only its initial letter

blocks.note: a base is where you live or operate from
the initial letter
the initial letter
I is the symbol for electric current, the word reduced to one letter

explanation.surface: A dogs' home faces closure because of funding cuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dog's home' reads as a kennel, but the apostrophe-s is 'is' linking the definition. I is the physics symbol for current.
explanation.definitionFit: The basenji is a small central African hunting breed known for yodelling instead of barking.

clue.text: Israeli reported just in time to be starting reduced legal procedure used in self-defence

indicators.note: a report is spoken word, so this piece is taken by its sound
the start of each word is its opening letter, which is all that is kept
reducing something makes it shorter, so letters are dropped from the end

blocks.note: an Israeli is often a Jew; the sound is spelt a different way
the initial letters of three words
a suit, a lawsuit, with its last two letters dropped

explanation.surface: An Israeli arrived just in time for a trimmed-down court case about self-defence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just in time' reads as a phrase about punctuality, but it provides three initial letters. A legal procedure is a suit, cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: Jiu-jitsu is a Japanese martial art of grappling and throws, practised as a method of self-protection.

clue.text: Revolutionary audacity turns out to be  reactionary

blocks.note: a red is a communist revolutionary
neck is British slang for cheek or nerve

explanation.surface: A radical's boldness proves, ironically, to be conservative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' suggests a reversal, but it is just RED. Having the neck to do something is British slang for having the nerve.
explanation.definitionFit: A redneck is a derogatory term for a rural, ultra-conservative white American, a reactionary type.

clue.text: Catalpa to remain — imagine a leading racecourse without one

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the named letter is taken away

blocks.note: to be is to exist, to stay as one is
Aintree near Liverpool hosts the Grand National
the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone muses on keeping a tree beside a top racecourse.
explanation.walkthrough: Aintree is the English course that stages the Grand National steeplechase; take out its I. 'Imagine' just invites you to think of the course.
explanation.definitionFit: The catalpa is commonly called the Indian bean tree because of its long, bean-like seed pods.

clue.text: Itches to restore a code of morals

indicators.note: restoring something means rebuilding it, so the letters are put back together differently

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone longs to bring back proper standards of conduct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Itches' reads as a verb meaning longs, but it is the letters to rework.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethics are the principles of right and wrong that govern a person's or profession's behaviour.

clue.text: Sir Harry was heard on the 11 25

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for a pouch found on the alimentary canal

indicators.note: something heard is taken in by the ear, so the name counts by its sound only

blocks.note: Sir Harry Secombe was a Welsh comedian and singer, one of the Goons

explanation.surface: A knighted entertainer's voice was heard on a famous British waterway.
explanation.walkthrough: Harry Secombe was a much-loved British entertainer from The Goon Show; his surname is said SEE-kum, like the gut pouch.
explanation.definitionFit: The caecum is the blind pouch where the small intestine joins the large, so it lies on the digestive tract.

clue.text: Lamentable that new garden city not given date letters

indicators.note: what is not given is withheld, so part of the fodder is left out
making something new means remaking it, so what remains is rebuilt in a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written
these four letters come out

explanation.surface: It's a shame that a planned new town has not been given a completion date.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove D, A, T and E from 'garden city', wherever they sit, and rearrange what is left. A garden city is a British planned town such as Welwyn.
explanation.definitionFit: A crying shame is one that is deplorable, so crying here means lamentable or grievous.

clue.text: Drink with arch criminal — a gang leader, indeed

indicators.note: something criminal is crooked and bent, so these letters are twisted out of shape

blocks.note: the four letters rearranged
a mafia boss is a don
nay in its old sense of 'and indeed', as in 'good, nay excellent'

explanation.surface: A mobster sharing a drink with his arch-villain rival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arch criminal' reads as one phrase, a master villain; 'criminal' actually works on 'arch' alone. Nay can mean 'indeed, even more', introducing a stronger word.
explanation.definitionFit: Chardonnay is a popular white wine made from the grape of the same name, a drink.

clue.text: Futile state to get in

blocks.note: the postal abbreviation for Virginia
taken as written

explanation.surface: It's pointless trying to gain entry to some country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' could be a condition, but here it is a US state abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: An effort made in vain is useless and achieves nothing, so vain means pointless.

clue.text: Turn against at all times

blocks.note: v for versus
e'er, the poetic contraction of ever

explanation.surface: Someone is permanently opposed to something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn against' reads as one phrasal verb, but 'Turn' stands alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To veer is to change direction abruptly, to swing aside from a course.

clue.text: See 11
Contract is a swindle — extremely stupid to go along with it

blocks.note: a con is a trick or fraud
dense means very slow-witted

explanation.surface: A business agreement is a scam, and you'd be a fool to sign it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contract' looks like the noun for a legal agreement, but it is the verb meaning shrink.
explanation.definitionFit: To condense something is to make it smaller or more compact, to shrink or compress it.
